appMenuEditor.description: Group and order what the App shows. Everyone only sees the entries they may open; an empty group is hidden.
appMenuEditor.emptyDescription: Published DataViews and Dashboards appear here.
appMenuEditor.dropAtEnd: Drop here to put it at the end of the menu
appMenuEditor.sortByNameDescription: Sorts the whole menu by name, inside every group and subgroup too - groups first. Replaces the current order.
appMenuEditor.sortByTypeDescription: Sorts the whole menu by type, then by name, inside every group and subgroup too - groups first, by name. Replaces the current order.
appMenuEditor.hiddenDescription: Published, but not in the menu or the App's lists. They keep working where they are embedded and open by their link.
appMenuEditor.descriptionHelp: The DataView's own description - shown in the menu on hover.
appMenuEditor.groupIconOpenHelp: While the group is open. Empty: its icon in both states - a folder that opens when it has none.
appMenuEditor.labelHelp: Empty: its name, {name}. Applies at once - no publish.
appMenuEditor.deleteGroupHelp: Its entries and subgroups move up a level - nothing is deleted.
appMenuEditor.removeFromMenuHelp: It stays as it is, out of the menu (Hidden, below) - deleting it is in its settings.
appMenuEditor.openStateHelp: How this group starts in the tree menu - the one holding the current page always opens.
appMenuEditor.searchBoxHelp: Over the menu - by an entry's label, full name, description or group. Automatic: once a viewer sees more than 15 entries. "/" brings it from any screen.

authProviders.title: Providers
authProviders.description: Google, GitHub or any OIDC provider your app's users can sign in with.

steps.providerDescription: Who your users sign in with.

authProviders.fillField: Fill in the field above to continue
authProviders.emptyDescription: Let your app's users sign in with Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Okta or any OIDC provider. TotalBase handles the OAuth exchange; your app links here and reads a session token back.
authProviders.clientRequired: Client ID and client secret are required
authProviders.redirectRequired: Add at least one allowed redirect URL
authProviders.issuerRequired: Issuer is required for an OIDC provider
authProviders.noExtraConfig: {provider} needs no extra configuration - continue to credentials.
authProviders.issuerDescription: Its OpenID discovery document must be reachable at {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration.
authProviders.redirectUriDescription: Register this exact URL as the provider's authorized redirect URI (e.g. in the Google Cloud Console or your GitHub OAuth App settings).
authProviders.deleteBody: This permanently deletes the following providers. Users who signed in through one keep their account - only their linked identity for that provider is removed, so they'll need to sign in a different way. This cannot be undone.
authProviders.clientSecretDescription: References a secret created under Settings > Secrets - the plaintext value is never shown here.
authProviders.noSecrets: No secrets exist yet - create one under Settings → Secrets first.
authProviders.allowedRedirectsDescription: Where a caller's own app may be sent back to after login, e.g. https://app.example.com/callback. An entry ending in /* matches anything under that prefix.
authProviders.defaultRoleDescription: Assigned only to a brand-new user's first login through this provider - never changes an existing user's roles.

tenantId.label: Tenant ID
tenantId.description: Use "common" to accept any Microsoft account, or a specific tenant GUID to restrict to one organization.

issuer.label: Issuer
issuer.description: e.g. https://issuer.example.com - its OpenID discovery document must be reachable at {'{'}issuer{'}'}/.well-known/openid-configuration.

authProviders.showOnSignInDescription: A button on the portal's sign-in page; people sign in to the admin or the App with this provider. Its own callback needs no allowed redirect URL.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.description: Size and vacuum state of every table, from PostgreSQL's own statistics.

plans.vacuumDeadNote: {n} table has no dead rows and is left out. The count comes from PostgreSQL's statistics, which start from zero again if they are reset. | {n} tables have no dead rows and are left out. The count comes from PostgreSQL's statistics, which start from zero again if they are reset.
plans.analyzeNeverNote: Gives the query planner row estimates for tables it has none for yet.
plans.reindexNote: Rebuilds {size} of indexes, one at a time - each needs about its own size in free disk space while it's rebuilt.

maintenance.ownedByLocked: Owned by {owner} - TotalBase's role can't maintain it
maintenance.cantMaintainTitle: TotalBase's role can't maintain this table
maintenance.cantMaintainDescription: It belongs to {owner}. Only its owner can VACUUM, ANALYZE or REINDEX it - or, on PostgreSQL 17+, a role granted MAINTAIN on it.
maintenance.operationsHelp: Vacuum reclaims dead rows and refreshes the planner's statistics; Analyze only refreshes the statistics; Reindex rebuilds every index concurrently. They run in the background without blocking the table.
maintenance.neverUsed: never used since the statistics were reset

maintenanceBatch.previewTargets: target, one at a time in the background. Tables stay readable and writable throughout. | targets, one at a time in the background. Tables stay readable and writable throughout.
maintenanceBatch.skipped: Skipped - TotalBase's role can't maintain it: | Skipped - TotalBase's role can't maintain them:
maintenanceBatch.stopPending: The {n} not started yet will be cancelled.
maintenanceBatch.stopReindex: The index being rebuilt finishes first - stopping it midway would leave an invalid index.
maintenanceBatch.stopTable: The table in progress stops too; nothing is left half done.

asyncExecutions.title: Executions
asyncExecutions.description: The PostgreSQL-backed queues TotalBase works through in the background: executions, and the data events that start DATA_EVENT workflows.

connector.title: Connector
connector.description: How TotalBase connects to PostgreSQL, and how it follows changes to your schema.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.description: Multi-operation transactions and Idempotency-Key replay for Data API writes.

groupForm.noSecrets: No secrets yet - create one under {link}.
groupForm.restartPending: Saved - the server still runs with {value} until it restarts.

appMenu.nothingPublished: Nothing is published for you yet.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Encrypted, write-only credentials, referenced by key.
secrets.emptyDescription: Store a credential once - an SMTP password, an OAuth client secret - and reference it by key. Values can be replaced, never read back.
secrets.keyValueRequired: Key and value are both required
secrets.deleteFailures: {n} failed - still referenced elsewhere, most likely.
secrets.keyDescription: Lowercase, letters/numbers with '.', '_', or '-' separators, e.g. 'afip-bearer-token' or 'mail.password'.

generator.title: Generate a value
generator.copyFailed: Could not copy - select it and copy it by hand
generator.copyNow: Copy it now - once saved it is never shown again.

secrets.deleteBody: If any Auth Provider or other reference still points at one of these secrets, its deletion will be rejected - remove or repoint that reference first. This cannot be undone.

smtp.connectionWorksDescription: The SMTP server accepted the connection and the credentials.
smtp.unreachable: Could not reach the SMTP server.
smtp.sendFailed: Could not send the test email.
smtp.sendToDescription: Uses the saved settings - save any change first.

s3.connectionWorksDescription: A test file was written to the bucket, read back and deleted.
s3.unreachable: Could not reach the S3 service.

api.label: Limits
api.description: Limits and defaults applied to every request through TotalBase's generic table API.

query.label: Query features
query.description: Query language features Data API callers may use.

api_keys.label: Tokens
api_keys.description: Defaults applied when a personal API token is issued without its own explicit values.

files.label: Files
files.description: Upload limits and on-the-fly image transformation settings for the Files explorer.

audit.label: Audit
audit.description: What gets recorded to the audit log, and for how long it's kept.

system.label: General
system.description: This instance's name and logo, public address, and how it shows dates and times.

auth.label: Authentication
auth.description: Account registration, session lifetime, and password policy for TotalBase users.

smtp.label: SMTP
smtp.description: The mail relay for system emails and Workflow "Send email" steps.

s3.label: S3 storage
s3.description: A connection to an S3-compatible bucket - Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO and others - where Files can store uploads.

security.label: Network
security.description: Rate limiting, CORS, and reverse-proxy trust settings for the public API.

pool.label: Connection pool
pool.description: The PostgreSQL connections TotalBase keeps open. Applies after a server restart.

catalog.label: Schema sync
catalog.description: How TotalBase keeps its resources in step with your PostgreSQL schema.

openapi.label: OpenAPI
openapi.description: The Data API document generated from your schema, permissions and workflows.

sql_console.label: SQL Console
sql_console.description: Whether admins can run raw SQL, how much of a result it shows, and how long its history is kept.

dataviews.label: DataViews
dataviews.description: The toolbar every list DataView opens with, how wide its pages grow, and row caps for exporting, printing and the MAP, KANBAN, CALENDAR and GANTT layouts.

workflows.label: Workflows
workflows.description: Execution limits and history retention for the Workflows engine.

dashboards.label: Dashboards
dashboards.description: Limits on the read-only SQL queries behind dashboard widgets, and embedding dashboards in other sites.

maps.label: Maps
maps.description: The tiles every map draws - MAP DataViews, map fields and dashboard maps.

app.label: App
app.description: How the App shows its menu of published DataViews and Dashboards.

transactions.label: Transactions
transactions.description: Several Data API operations committed or rolled back as one PostgreSQL transaction.

idempotency.label: Idempotency
idempotency.description: Idempotency-Key replay, so a retried write runs only once.

async_executions.label: Executions
async_executions.description: The PostgreSQL-backed queue that runs executions in the background, with retries.

outbox.label: Data events
outbox.description: The outbox of committed data changes that starts DATA_EVENT workflows: retries and retention.

appearance.label: Appearance
appearance.description: How this instance looks to everyone - its color, its sign-in page and any CSS of your own. Public: all of it reaches the browser before sign-in.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.description: The MCP server an AI agent builds and operates this instance through - served at this instance's own address, /mcp, with an administrator's token.

backups.label: Backups
backups.description: Scheduled backups of the database and the stored files, kept on the local disk or in S3 storage. The master key is never in them - keep it apart.

api__default_limit.label: Default page size
api__default_limit.description: Rows returned by a list request that doesn't specify its own limit.

api__max_limit.label: Maximum page size
api__max_limit.description: The largest limit a caller is allowed to request, regardless of what they ask for.

api__max_offset.label: Maximum offset
api__max_offset.description: Caps how deep offset-based pagination can page into a result set.

api__max_relation_depth.label: Maximum relation depth
api__max_relation_depth.description: How many foreign keys a dotted path may follow in one request (order.customer.email follows two).

api__max_filter_depth.label: Maximum filter depth
api__max_filter_depth.description: How deeply nested a filter expression (and/or groups) is allowed to be.

api__require_where_for_update.label: Require a filter for bulk update
api__require_where_for_update.description: Blocks a bulk UPDATE that has no WHERE clause - through the Data API or a workflow's Update records step - to prevent accidentally updating every row.

api__require_where_for_delete.label: Require a filter for bulk delete
api__require_where_for_delete.description: Blocks a bulk DELETE that has no WHERE clause - through the Data API or a workflow's Delete records step - to prevent accidentally deleting every row.

api__bulk_max_items.label: Maximum bulk items
api__bulk_max_items.description: The most rows a single bulk create/update/delete request can touch at once.

api__max_body_bytes.label: Maximum request body size
api__max_body_bytes.description: Requests with a larger body are rejected before they're parsed.

api__max_query_string_bytes.label: Maximum query string size
api__max_query_string_bytes.description: Requests with a longer query string are rejected before they're parsed. Raising it above the value the server started with takes a restart.

api__max_query_parameters.label: Maximum query parameters
api__max_query_parameters.description: The most query-string parameters a single request is allowed to send.

api__max_query_nodes.label: Maximum query nodes
api__max_query_nodes.description: Caps the total complexity (filter/sort/expand nodes combined) of a single request.

api__nested_write_max_depth.label: Maximum nested write depth
api__nested_write_max_depth.description: How many levels deep a single CREATE can nest child records (parent → child → grandchild).

api__nested_write_max_records.label: Maximum nested write records
api__nested_write_max_records.description: The most records a single nested create can insert across all levels combined.

api__request_timeout_ms.label: Request timeout
api__request_timeout_ms.description: Longest a single Data API request's SQL may run - PostgreSQL cancels it past this and the caller gets QUERY_CANCELED.

api__allow_count.label: Allow count
api__allow_count.description: Lets a list request ask for the total number of matching rows (count=true) - an extra query over the whole filtered set.

query__allow_regex.label: Allow regular expressions
query__allow_regex.description: Lets filters use _regex. A regular expression can't use an ordinary index, so it scans every row it's applied to.

query__allow_contains.label: Allow containment operators
query__allow_contains.description: Lets filters use _contains, _contained_by and _overlap on arrays and jsonb - fast with a GIN index, a full scan without one.

query__allow_having.label: Allow having
query__allow_having.description: Lets grouped queries filter on their aggregates (having), after grouping every matching row.

api_keys__default_ttl_days.label: Default expiry
api_keys__default_ttl_days.description: How long a newly issued API key is valid for, if the request doesn't set its own expiry.

api_keys__rotation_warning_days.label: Rotation warning window
api_keys__rotation_warning_days.description: How far ahead of expiry an API key is flagged as "expiring soon" in the admin.

api_keys__purge_after_days.label: Keep ended tokens
api_keys__purge_after_days.description: Revoked and expired tokens stay listed for this long after they end, then are deleted. A deactivated token is kept - it can be turned on again. 0 keeps them forever.

files__enabled.label: Enable Files
files__enabled.description: Turns the Files explorer upload and storage feature on or off.

files__max_file_size_bytes.label: Maximum file size
files__max_file_size_bytes.description: The largest single file an upload is allowed to be.

files__allowed_mime_types.label: Allowed file types
files__allowed_mime_types.description: MIME types accepted on upload. Wildcards such as text/* and image/* are supported.

files__default_visibility_public.label: Public by default
files__default_visibility_public.description: Whether a newly uploaded file starts as public when the upload form does not choose otherwise.

files__storage_provider.label: Storage provider
files__storage_provider.description: Where new uploads are stored. A file already uploaded stays where it was written and is still served from there. S3 storage must be enabled first.

files__storage_local_path.label: Local storage path
files__storage_local_path.description: Where local files are kept - including those uploaded before switching to S3 storage, still served from here.

files__transforms__enabled.label: Enable image transforms
files__transforms__enabled.description: Turns on-the-fly image resizing/format conversion on or off.

files__transforms__max_width.label: Maximum output width
files__transforms__max_width.description: The widest an on-the-fly transformed image is allowed to be.

files__transforms__max_height.label: Maximum output height
files__transforms__max_height.description: The tallest an on-the-fly transformed image is allowed to be.

files__transforms__max_pixels.label: Maximum total pixels
files__transforms__max_pixels.description: Caps width × height together, on top of the individual width/height limits.

files__transforms__max_concurrent.label: Maximum concurrent transforms
files__transforms__max_concurrent.description: How many image transforms are allowed to run at the same time.

files__transforms__timeout_ms.label: Transform timeout
files__transforms__timeout_ms.description: A transform that takes longer than this is aborted.

files__transforms__cache_ttl_seconds.label: Transform cache lifetime
files__transforms__cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long browsers may cache a transformed image, and how long its stored copy is kept before the hourly cleanup removes it (the next request regenerates it).

files__transforms__max_operations.label: Maximum operations per transform
files__transforms__max_operations.description: The most chained operations (resize, crop, format, ...) a single transform request can request.

files__transforms__presets_json.label: Named presets (JSON)
files__transforms__presets_json.description: A raw JSON object of named transform presets, e.g. {'{'}"thumbnail":{'{'}"width":150,"height":150,"fit":"cover","format":"webp","quality":80{'}'}{'}'}.

audit__enabled.label: Enable audit logging
audit__enabled.description: Turns audit logging on or off for the whole system.

audit__retention_days.label: Retention period
audit__retention_days.description: Audit log entries older than this are purged automatically, hourly. 0 keeps them forever.

audit__store_sql.label: Store SQL statements
audit__store_sql.description: Whether the audit log keeps the actual SQL statement executed for each write.

audit__store_sql_params.label: Store SQL parameters
audit__store_sql_params.description: Whether the audit log also keeps the bound parameter values, not just the statement shape.

auth__registration_enabled.label: Allow self-registration
auth__registration_enabled.description: Lets a new user create their own account instead of requiring an admin invitation.

auth__registration_default_role.label: Default role for self-registration
auth__registration_default_role.description: Given to every account created through self-registration. None: a new account has no roles until someone assigns one.

auth__email_verification_required.label: Require email verification
auth__email_verification_required.description: A newly registered account can't sign in until its email address is verified.

auth__password_min_length.label: Minimum password length
auth__password_min_length.description: The shortest password TotalBase will accept when a user sets or changes theirs.

auth__session_ttl_hours.label: Session lifetime
auth__session_ttl_hours.description: How long a signed-in session stays valid before it needs to sign in again.

auth__session_idle_minutes.label: Sign out after inactivity
auth__session_idle_minutes.description: A session unused this long ends, and its user signs in again - for shared or unattended computers. 0 keeps a session until its lifetime ends.

auth__password_reset_ttl_minutes.label: Password reset link lifetime
auth__password_reset_ttl_minutes.description: How long a "reset your password" link stays valid after it's sent.

auth__email_verification_ttl_hours.label: Email verification link lifetime
auth__email_verification_ttl_hours.description: How long a "verify your email" link stays valid after it's sent.

auth__invitation_ttl_hours.label: Invitation lifetime
auth__invitation_ttl_hours.description: How long an admin-sent invitation link stays valid before it expires.

auth__max_sessions_per_user.label: Maximum sessions per user
auth__max_sessions_per_user.description: The most devices/browsers a single user can be signed in on at once.

auth__session_retention_days.label: Keep ended sessions
auth__session_retention_days.description: Revoked and expired sessions stay listed (Sessions → Revoked / Expired) for this long after they end, then are deleted. 0 keeps them forever.

auth__lockout_max_attempts.label: Lock after failed sign-ins
auth__lockout_max_attempts.description: Consecutive wrong passwords that lock the account for a while. The person sees the usual "invalid email or password" either way; an admin can unlock them early. 0 turns lockout off.

auth__dormant_account_days.label: Deactivate unused accounts
auth__dormant_account_days.description: An account with no sign-in, no session and no token used for this many days is deactivated - someone who left, an account nobody remembered. The owner never is. 0 turns it off.

auth__reauthentication_minutes.label: Confirm identity for sensitive actions
auth__reauthentication_minutes.description: How long after signing in, or confirming their password again, an administrator can issue an administrator token, assign Administrators, or change another account's email, password or two-factor authentication. Past it, they're asked for their password (or a code) first.

auth__lockout_duration_minutes.label: Lockout duration
auth__lockout_duration_minutes.description: How long a locked account stays locked. A password reset or an admin's unlock ends it sooner.

auth__mfa_required.label: Require two-factor authentication
auth__mfa_required.description: Who must sign in with a code from an authenticator app. Someone required who hasn't set it up is asked to at their next sign-in; sessions already open stay.

auth__links__invitation.label: Invitation link
auth__links__invitation.description: Where an invitation email's link points. {'{'}{'{'}public_url{'}'}{'}'} and {'{'}{'{'}token{'}'}{'}'} are filled in by TotalBase - point it at your own app's page if it handles invitations itself.

auth__links__password_reset.label: Password reset link
auth__links__password_reset.description: Where a password reset email's link points. Same {'{'}{'{'}public_url{'}'}{'}'} and {'{'}{'{'}token{'}'}{'}'} placeholders.

auth__links__email_verification.label: Email verification link
auth__links__email_verification.description: Where an email verification link points. Same {'{'}{'{'}public_url{'}'}{'}'} and {'{'}{'{'}token{'}'}{'}'} placeholders.

auth__password_changed_email_enabled.label: Password changed notice
auth__password_changed_email_enabled.description: Email the account owner whenever their password is changed or reset - a security notice.

auth__email_changed_email_enabled.label: Email changed notice
auth__email_changed_email_enabled.description: Email the previous address whenever an admin changes a user's email - a security notice.

auth__mfa_disabled_email_enabled.label: Two-factor turned off notice
auth__mfa_disabled_email_enabled.description: Email the account owner whenever their two-factor authentication is turned off, or reset by an admin - a security notice.

auth__token_created_email_enabled.label: New API token notice
auth__token_created_email_enabled.description: Email the account owner whenever an API token is created or regenerated for them - a security notice.

auth__welcome_email_enabled.label: Welcome email
auth__welcome_email_enabled.description: Email a welcome message once an invited or registered account is ready to use.

system__public_url.label: Public URL
system__public_url.description: The final address people reach this instance at, e.g. https://totalbase.example.com - invitation, password reset and OAuth links are built from it. Leave empty to use the TOTALBASE_PUBLIC_URL environment variable.

system__instance_name.label: Instance name
system__instance_name.description: How this instance names itself in the emails it sends.

system__logo.label: Logo
system__logo.description: Your mark in place of TotalBase's, beside the instance's name - in the rail, on the sign-in page and on the public pages - shown at the mark's height, so a wide or a square image both work. A public image in Files; PNG or SVG with transparency looks best.

system__timezone.label: Timezone
system__timezone.description: The organization's zone: timestamptz values are shown in it, and reports and filters such as "this month" count days in it - for every user who didn't choose their own. Empty = each viewer's browser timezone.

system__timezone_user_choice.label: Users can choose their own timezone
system__timezone_user_choice.description: Off: everyone works in the Timezone above - a user's own choice is kept, not used, until this is on again. Needs a Timezone set: with none, each viewer's browser decides.

system__date_format.label: Default date format
system__date_format.description: date-fns pattern (e.g. dd/MM/yyyy) dates are shown in, for every user who didn't choose their own. Empty = the browser's format.

system__time_format.label: Default time format
system__time_format.description: date-fns pattern (e.g. HH:mm) times are shown in, for every user who didn't choose their own. Empty = the browser's format.

system__datetime_format.label: Default date/time format
system__datetime_format.description: date-fns pattern (e.g. dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm) dates with a time are shown in, for users who chose neither a date nor a time format. Empty = the browser's format.

system__language.label: Default language
system__language.description: The language of the interface for users who didn't choose one in My account, and of pages with no signed-in user - sign-in, password reset, embedded dashboards. Data and PostgreSQL's messages are never translated.

smtp__host.label: SMTP host
smtp__host.description: Hostname of the outgoing mail relay. Empty means SMTP isn't configured - sending fails until this is set.

smtp__port.label: SMTP port
smtp__port.description: Port to connect to on the SMTP host - typically 587 (STARTTLS) or 465 (implicit TLS).

smtp__secure.label: Use implicit TLS
smtp__secure.description: Connect over TLS from the start (port 465-style) instead of upgrading via STARTTLS.

smtp__username.label: SMTP username
smtp__username.description: Username to authenticate with the SMTP relay. Leave empty for a relay that doesn't require auth.

smtp__password_secret_key.label: SMTP password (secret key)
smtp__password_secret_key.description: The key of a Settings → Secrets entry holding the SMTP password - never stored here in plaintext. Leave empty for a relay that doesn't require auth.

smtp__from.label: From address
smtp__from.description: The envelope/header From address outgoing mail is sent as.

s3__enabled.label: Enable S3 storage
s3__enabled.description: Turns the connection on. Can't be turned off while Files stores new uploads in it or still holds files there.

s3__endpoint.label: Endpoint
s3__endpoint.description: The service's base URL, e.g. https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com or http://minio:9000.

s3__region.label: Region
s3__region.description: The bucket's region, part of every request's signature - us-east-1 for most services that don't have regions, auto for Cloudflare R2.

s3__bucket.label: Bucket
s3__bucket.description: The bucket to write to. It must exist; TotalBase doesn't create it.

s3__prefix.label: Key prefix
s3__prefix.description: A folder inside the bucket for this instance, e.g. production/ - so several instances can share one bucket. Each use writes under its own folder in it (files/). Empty: the bucket's root.

s3__path_style.label: Path-style addressing
s3__path_style.description: Address the bucket as endpoint/bucket instead of bucket.endpoint - MinIO and most self-hosted services need it on.

s3__access_key_id.label: Access key ID
s3__access_key_id.description: The access key's ID. Its secret goes in the next setting, as a secret.

s3__secret_key.label: Secret access key (secret key)
s3__secret_key.description: The key of a Settings → Secrets entry holding the secret access key - never stored here in plaintext.

security__rate_limit_enabled.label: Enable rate limiting
security__rate_limit_enabled.description: Limits the requests and the failed sign-ins of each IP address. Behind a proxy, turn on Trust reverse proxy headers with it - otherwise every caller has the proxy's address and shares one limit.

security__rate_limit_per_minute.label: Requests per minute
security__rate_limit_per_minute.description: The most requests one IP address can make in a one-minute window before being throttled.

security__rate_limit_sign_in_per_minute.label: Failed sign-ins per minute
security__rate_limit_sign_in_per_minute.description: The most failed sign-in attempts from one IP address in a minute - a correct sign-in doesn't count. Each account also locks after its own failed attempts, in Access.

security__cors_enabled.label: Enable CORS
security__cors_enabled.description: Allows browser requests to the API from the origins listed below.

security__cors_origins.label: Allowed origins
security__cors_origins.description: Origins (e.g. https://app.example.com) allowed to call the API directly from a browser.

security__trust_proxy.label: Trust reverse proxy headers
security__trust_proxy.description: Reads the caller's real IP from X-Forwarded-For - only enable this behind a proxy you control. Applies after a restart.

auth__access_review_interval_days.label: Access review interval
auth__access_review_interval_days.description: How often the Administrators role's members should be reviewed - the role shows a review as due once its last one is older than this. 0 turns the reminder off.

transactions__enabled.label: Enable transactions
transactions__enabled.description: Allows POST /api/transactions - a role still needs its own transactions.execute grant to use it.

transactions__max_operations.label: Maximum operations
transactions__max_operations.description: The most operations a single transaction request can contain.

transactions__timeout_ms.label: Statement timeout
transactions__timeout_ms.description: How long one statement of a transaction may run before PostgreSQL cancels it (and the whole transaction rolls back). 0 uses the Data API's request timeout.

idempotency__enabled.label: Enable idempotency keys
idempotency__enabled.description: Honors the Idempotency-Key header on writes - a retry with the same key replays the first response instead of running again.

idempotency__ttl_hours.label: Key lifetime
idempotency__ttl_hours.description: How long a key and its stored response are kept - a retry after this runs as a new request.

idempotency__max_response_bytes.label: Maximum stored response
idempotency__max_response_bytes.description: Larger responses aren't stored for replay - the write still runs only once, but a retry gets an error instead of the original body.

async_executions__enabled.label: Enable the worker
async_executions__enabled.description: Turns off background processing - queued executions wait until it's enabled again.

async_executions__max_retries.label: Maximum retries
async_executions__max_retries.description: How many times a failed execution is retried, when its failure is retryable, before it's marked failed.

async_executions__retry_delay_seconds.label: Retry delay
async_executions__retry_delay_seconds.description: How long a failed execution waits before its next attempt.

async_executions__stale_timeout_ms.label: Stale timeout
async_executions__stale_timeout_ms.description: An execution still running after this is treated as abandoned by a crashed worker and picked up again.

async_executions__poll_interval_ms.label: Poll interval
async_executions__poll_interval_ms.description: How often the worker checks the queue for new work.

async_executions__retention_days.label: Keep finished executions
async_executions__retention_days.description: Completed, failed and cancelled executions stay queryable by their id for this long after they end, then are deleted. 0 keeps them forever.

outbox__retention_days.label: Processed event retention
outbox__retention_days.description: Data events already handed to their workflows are deleted after this long. Failed events that ran out of attempts are kept.

outbox__max_attempts.label: Maximum attempts
outbox__max_attempts.description: How many times a data event is dispatched before it stays failed.

outbox__retry_delay_seconds.label: Retry delay
outbox__retry_delay_seconds.description: The wait before a failed data event is retried - doubled after each further attempt.

outbox__lease_seconds.label: Processing lease
outbox__lease_seconds.description: How long a data event being handed to its workflows is held before it counts as abandoned (its process stopped) and is retried. Keep it above the longest workflow run.

pool__max.label: Maximum connections
pool__max.description: The most connections open at once. Keep it under the database's max_connections, shared with every other client. Applies after a restart.

pool__idle_timeout_ms.label: Idle timeout
pool__idle_timeout_ms.description: An unused connection is closed after this long. Applies after a restart.

pool__connection_timeout_ms.label: Connection timeout
pool__connection_timeout_ms.description: How long a request waits for a free connection (or a new one to open) before failing. Applies after a restart.

pool__max_lifetime_ms.label: Maximum connection lifetime
pool__max_lifetime_ms.description: A connection is replaced after this long, however busy - lets a load balancer or failover rebalance. 0 = never. Applies after a restart.

catalog__watch_interval_seconds.label: Watch for schema changes
catalog__watch_interval_seconds.description: How often TotalBase checks whether the schema changed outside it (psql, a migration tool), and syncs at once when it did. 0 = off.

catalog__refresh_interval_minutes.label: Scheduled sync
catalog__refresh_interval_minutes.description: How often TotalBase re-reads the whole schema, whatever the change check found - the safety net for what it can't see. 0 = off.

catalog__auto_refresh_after_ddl.label: Sync after SQL Console runs
catalog__auto_refresh_after_ddl.description: Re-reads the schema after every SQL Console run, so a table it creates or drops shows up at once. The table editor always syncs.

catalog__track_comments.label: Sync descriptions with COMMENT ON
catalog__track_comments.description: Fills a resource's empty description from PostgreSQL's COMMENT ON, and an empty comment from the description, on every sync.

openapi__enabled.label: Publish the OpenAPI document
openapi__enabled.description: Serves /api/openapi.json to API callers, showing what their own roles can reach. Off = 404; admins still see it under Docs.

openapi__include_examples.label: Include example values
openapi__include_examples.description: Adds a sample value to every column and argument, for tools that show or generate requests from the document.

openapi__cache_enabled.label: Cache generated documents
openapi__cache_enabled.description: Keeps each role set's document until the schema, permissions, workflows or settings change, instead of rebuilding it on every request.

sql_console__enabled.label: Enable SQL Console
sql_console__enabled.description: Lets admins run raw SQL from the console. Off = the console can't execute or explain; its history stays readable.

sql_console__token_access.label: Allow API tokens
sql_console__token_access.description: Lets an administrator's personal access token run SQL - the MCP server's agent, a script. Off = only a signed-in administrator. Changed from here only, never by a token.

sql_console__max_rows.label: Result row cap
sql_console__max_rows.description: The most rows a query shows in the console - the query still runs in full; extra rows are left out of the result.

sql_console__history_retention_days.label: History retention
sql_console__history_retention_days.description: How long a query stays in the SQL Console's history before it's purged automatically.

dataviews__export_max_rows.label: Export row cap
dataviews__export_max_rows.description: The most rows the "All matching rows" scope will fetch when exporting a DataView (CSV/Excel). Extra matching rows beyond this are silently dropped, with a warning shown to whoever ran the export.

dataviews__export_warning_threshold.label: Export warning threshold
dataviews__export_warning_threshold.description: Row count above which exporting "All matching rows" shows a "this can take a few seconds" warning before running. Also used for the same warning when importing a large file.

dataviews__print_max_rows.label: Print row cap
dataviews__print_max_rows.description: The most rows the "All matching rows" scope will fetch when printing a DataView to PDF. Extra matching rows beyond this are silently dropped, with a warning shown to whoever ran the print.

dataviews__print_warning_threshold.label: Print warning threshold
dataviews__print_warning_threshold.description: Row count above which printing "All matching rows" shows a "this can take a few seconds" warning before running.

dataviews__map_max_points.label: Map point cap
dataviews__map_max_points.description: The most rows a MAP DataView plots at once (it has no pager - every relevant pin loads up front). Extra matching rows beyond this aren't fetched, with a notice shown on the map.

dataviews__kanban_max_cards.label: Kanban card cap
dataviews__kanban_max_cards.description: The most rows a KANBAN DataView loads at once, across every lane combined (it has no pager - every relevant card loads up front). Extra matching rows beyond this aren't fetched, with a notice shown on the board.

dataviews__calendar_max_events.label: Calendar event cap
dataviews__calendar_max_events.description: The most rows a CALENDAR DataView loads at once for the visible date range (it already fetches by month, not all-time - this is a defensive backstop for an unusually busy month). Extra matching rows beyond this aren't fetched, with a notice shown on the calendar.

dataviews__gantt_max_bars.label: Gantt bar cap
dataviews__gantt_max_bars.description: The most rows a GANTT DataView loads at once, across every lane combined (it has no pager - every relevant bar loads up front). Extra matching rows beyond this aren't fetched, with a notice shown on the timeline.

dataviews__tree_max_nodes.label: Tree node cap
dataviews__tree_max_nodes.description: The most rows a TREE DataView loads at once - the whole hierarchy, every level (it has no pager). Extra matching rows beyond this aren't fetched, with a notice shown on the tree.

dataviews__bulk_edit_max_rows.label: Bulk edit cap
dataviews__bulk_edit_max_rows.description: The most rows a viewer may choose and edit together - at most 100, the largest page a grid offers. Lower it to keep bulk edits smaller.

dataviews__save_max_operations.label: Record save cap
dataviews__save_max_operations.description: The most writes one save of a record and its lines makes - the header and every line added, changed or removed, all in one transaction. A save beyond it is refused whole.

maps__tiles.label: Map tiles
maps__tiles.description: What every map draws underneath - MAP DataViews, map fields and dashboard maps. Mapbox needs a public token below; without one, maps keep OpenStreetMap.

maps__mapbox_token.label: Mapbox public token
maps__mapbox_token.description: A public token (pk.…) from your Mapbox account, restricted there to this instance's URL - it is sent to every viewer's browser. A secret token (sk.…) is refused.

maps__default_view.label: Default map view
maps__default_view.description: Where an empty map field opens - latitude, longitude, zoom (e.g. -24.79, -65.41, 12 for Salta). Empty: the whole world.

maps__mapbox_style.label: Mapbox style
maps__mapbox_style.description: username/style_id - mapbox/streets-v12, mapbox/satellite-streets-v12, mapbox/light-v11, or a style of your own from Mapbox Studio.

app__menu_mode.label: Menu display
app__menu_mode.description: Tree: a collapsible hierarchy of groups. Sidebar: the same menu flat, each group a section heading.

dashboards__query_timeout_ms.label: Widget query timeout
dashboards__query_timeout_ms.description: Maximum time a dashboard widget's SQL may run (it always runs in a read-only transaction) before PostgreSQL cancels it.

dashboards__query_max_rows.label: Widget query row cap
dashboards__query_max_rows.description: The most rows a dashboard widget's SQL returns - extra rows are cut off, not paged.

dashboards__max_concurrent_queries.label: Widget queries at once
dashboards__max_concurrent_queries.description: How many widget queries of one dashboard run at the same time - the rest wait their turn, so a large dashboard never takes every connection the Data API needs.

dashboards__cache_seconds.label: Widget result cache
dashboards__cache_seconds.description: How long a published widget's result is reused for the same variables, viewer and time zone - unless its dashboard refreshes more often. Refresh skips it. 0 turns it off.

dashboards__embed_secret_key.label: Embedding secret
dashboards__embed_secret_key.description: The Settings → Secrets entry your site's backend signs embed tokens with (HS256) - it never reaches a browser. Empty: no dashboard can be embedded. Rotate it by creating a new secret and choosing it here; tokens signed with the old one stop working.

dashboards__embed_max_ttl_minutes.label: Longest embed token
dashboards__embed_max_ttl_minutes.description: A token whose expiry (exp) is further away than this is refused - keep embed tokens short-lived and sign a new one per page view.

dashboards__embed_allowed_origins.label: Sites that may embed
dashboards__embed_allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to frame an embedded dashboard (https://app.example.com) - sent as Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors. Empty: no site can frame one.

workflows__max_sync_wait_ms.label: Maximum synchronous wait
workflows__max_sync_wait_ms.description: The longest a WEBHOOK trigger's synchronous response mode will hold the connection open waiting for the run to finish, regardless of what an individual workflow's own wait time is configured to.

workflows__max_run_duration_ms.label: Maximum run duration
workflows__max_run_duration_ms.description: A run still executing past this is force-failed - the engine's own admission deadline, independent of any single step's own timeout.

workflows__max_operations_per_run.label: Maximum operations per run
workflows__max_operations_per_run.description: Caps the total number of steps (including loop iterations) a single run can execute before it's force-failed, to catch a runaway or accidentally-looping design.

workflows__max_iteration_items.label: Maximum iteration items
workflows__max_iteration_items.description: The most items a For each step's own collection can contain - a longer collection fails the step rather than iterating partially.

workflows__max_runtime_value_bytes.label: Maximum binding value size
workflows__max_runtime_value_bytes.description: Caps the size of any single resolved binding value (trigger data, a step's own result, an iteration item) - a larger value fails the step that tried to resolve it.

workflows__max_history_payload_bytes.label: Maximum history payload size
workflows__max_history_payload_bytes.description: Caps how much of a step's input/result is retained in DETAILED history - anything beyond this is truncated before it's persisted.

workflows__history_summary_retention_day.label: Summary history retention
workflows__history_summary_retention_day.description: How long a SUMMARY-level run's history (status and timing, no payloads) is kept before it's purged.

workflows__history_detailed_retention_da.label: Detailed history retention
workflows__history_detailed_retention_da.description: How long a DETAILED-level run's history (including redacted/capped step payloads) is kept before it's purged - shorter than summary retention by default, since it holds more sensitive data.

workflows__auto_disable_after_consecutiv.label: Auto-disable after consecutive failures
workflows__auto_disable_after_consecutiv.description: A workflow that fails this many runs in a row (of any trigger type) is automatically disabled - most useful for a CRON workflow, which would otherwise keep retrying forever with no external caller to notice.

workflows__max_chain_depth.label: Maximum chain depth
workflows__max_chain_depth.description: How many workflows one causal chain may hold - a workflow whose write starts another (data events) or that calls another (Execute workflow). A loop (A → A, A → B → A) is refused at any depth.

workflows__http_max_request_bytes.label: HTTP request maximum body
workflows__http_max_request_bytes.description: The largest body an HTTP request step may send. A larger one fails the step before anything is sent.

workflows__http_max_response_bytes.label: HTTP response maximum body
workflows__http_max_response_bytes.description: The largest response an HTTP request step reads. The transfer is cut once it goes past this, and the step fails.

workflows__http_allowed_hosts.label: HTTP request allowed hosts
workflows__http_allowed_hosts.description: Hostnames (api.internal.example), IP addresses or CIDR ranges (10.0.0.0/8) an HTTP request step may reach although they are private, loopback or link-local. Every other such destination is refused.

appearance__primary_color.label: Primary color
appearance__primary_color.description: The accent of every button, link and highlight. One color is enough: its lighter and darker shades are derived for light and dark mode. Empty keeps TotalBase's blue.

appearance__neutral_color.label: Neutral color
appearance__neutral_color.description: The grays of text, borders and backgrounds, in light and dark mode. Slate, TotalBase's own, leans blue - its dark mode too.

appearance__login_layout.label: Sign-in page
appearance__login_layout.description: What surrounds the sign-in card. Simple, Company panel and Image show your mark (Settings › General › General: your logo and name) and only a small "Powered by TotalBase" at the foot; on a phone they're the card under your mark (Image keeps its picture behind).

optionDescriptions.SPLIT: TotalBase's own panel - its headline, intro and features - beside the card.
optionDescriptions.SIMPLE: Your logo and name large and centered, your headline under them, the card below.
optionDescriptions.PANEL: A side panel with your logo, name, headline and intro - over the background image if there is one, else your primary color - beside the card. Nothing of TotalBase.
optionDescriptions.IMAGE: Your image across the page, your headline and intro over it, the card with your logo and name - left, center or right (Card position).

appearance__login_card_position.label: Card position
appearance__login_card_position.description: Where the Image layout's card sits on a wide screen - your headline and intro take the other side.

optionDescriptions.LEFT: The card on the left, your words on the right.
optionDescriptions.CENTER: The card in the middle, your headline above it.
optionDescriptions.RIGHT: Your words on the left, the card on the right.

appearance__login_background.label: Background image
appearance__login_background.description: The Image layout's background, and the Company panel's - a public image in Files, shown covering it. A photo of 1920 px or wider keeps sharp on a large screen.

appearance__login_headline.label: Headline
appearance__login_headline.description: Your words on the sign-in page: under your name (Simple), in the Company panel, over the Image layout's background. Up to 120 characters.

appearance__login_intro.label: Intro
appearance__login_intro.description: Under the headline, in the Company panel and the Image layout, on a wide screen. Up to 300 characters.

appearance__custom_css.label: Custom CSS
appearance__custom_css.description: Plain CSS applied last on every page - the admin, the App, sign-in, embeds. Stable to build on: Nuxt UI's tokens (--ui-primary, --ui-color-primary-*, --ui-bg, --ui-text, --ui-border, --ui-radius, --font-sans), .dark, and html[data-surface="app"] (admin, app, auth, embed) to target one surface, [data-shell="rail"], "panel", "header" or "main" for a part of the shell, and [data-shell="list"] with [data-dataview-type="TABLE"] (CARDS, KANBAN, CALENDAR, GANTT, MAP) for a DataView's list. Anything else may change between versions. No {'@'}import. If a rule hides the UI, open any page with ?safe-css to load without it.

mcp__enabled.label: Enable MCP
mcp__enabled.description: Serves the MCP server at this instance's address, /mcp, for an agent with an administrator's token. Off: /mcp doesn't answer, and the stdio binary refuses to start.

mcp__mode.label: Mode
mcp__mode.description: What an agent may do at all - on top of every permission TotalBase checks anyway.

optionDescriptions.READ_ONLY: Only tools that read: describe, list, query, get.
optionDescriptions.STANDARD: Build and change everything, but never delete or revoke - a destructive call is refused.
optionDescriptions.FULL: Everything, deletions included - each one still needs confirm=true.

mcp__tools_schema.label: Tables and schema
mcp__tools_schema.description: Create and change tables, schemas, columns' and rows' presentation, resources' exposure; describe them.

mcp__tools_records.label: Records
mcp__tools_records.description: Read and write rows of any exposed table - the application's and TotalBase's own - and call functions.

mcp__tools_access.label: Permissions
mcp__tools_access.description: Grant, revoke and read permissions; capabilities; default permissions.

mcp__tools_users.label: Users
mcp__tools_users.description: Create users with a password or an invitation, change their roles, send links.

mcp__tools_screens.label: DataViews and pages
mcp__tools_screens.description: Create, change, publish and delete DataViews, CUSTOM pages and the App menu.

mcp__tools_dashboards.label: Dashboards
mcp__tools_dashboards.description: Create, change, publish and delete dashboards and their widgets.

mcp__tools_workflows.label: Workflows
mcp__tools_workflows.description: Create, save, run, publish, enable and delete workflows.

mcp__tools_templates.label: Templates
mcp__tools_templates.description: Create, change and try email and PDF templates.

mcp__tools_sql.label: SQL
mcp__tools_sql.description: Raw SQL and its plans - also needs SQL Console's Allow API tokens.

mcp__instructions.label: Project instructions
mcp__instructions.description: Told to every agent with the server's own orientation - this project's conventions: names, language, its domain, what never to touch.

mcp__rate_limit_per_minute.label: Requests per minute
mcp__rate_limit_per_minute.description: The most MCP requests one token makes in a minute - each tool call is one. Its own calls to the APIs don't count toward Network's limit.

mcp__allowed_hosts.label: Allowed hosts
mcp__allowed_hosts.description: The Host a request to /mcp may name - refuses a page that tricks a browser into calling it (DNS rebinding). Empty: the public URL's host, and localhost.

dataviews__toolbar_mode.label: Toolbar
dataviews__toolbar_mode.description: How a list DataView's toolbar opens for someone who hasn't chosen - unless the DataView sets its own. Compact moves Search and the menu into the page header and tucks import, export, print, history and columns into the menu. A phone or tablet is always compact.

optionDescriptions.auto: Compact for CARDS, full for the other types.
optionDescriptions.full: Every action in a toolbar row.
optionDescriptions.compact: Search and the menu in the page header.

dataviews__record_content_width.label: Record page width
dataviews__record_content_width.description: How wide a record page's content grows - a FORM, a MASTER_DETAIL, a list's record opened on its own page - unless the DataView sets its own.

optionDescriptions.narrow: A readable column - a form of a few fields, a one-step screen.
optionDescriptions.wide: Room for two or three columns of fields.

dataviews__custom_content_width.label: CUSTOM page width
dataviews__custom_content_width.description: How wide a CUSTOM page's content and its pinned footer grow - unless the DataView sets its own.

optionDescriptions.narrow: A readable column - a form of a few fields, a one-step screen.
optionDescriptions.wide: Room for two or three columns of fields.

dataviews__content_align.label: Content align
dataviews__content_align.description: Where a page narrower than the screen sits - unless the DataView sets its own.

dataviews__table_margin.label: Table margin
dataviews__table_margin.description: The space around a TABLE's grid in the App, unless the DataView sets its own. Cards, maps, boards, calendars and timelines keep the normal margin; record pages, forms, pages and dashboards their own.

optionDescriptions.none: The table fills the page, right under its header.

app__menu_groups_open.label: Groups when the App opens
app__menu_groups_open.description: How the tree menu's groups start - a group may set its own. The one holding the page always opens; what each viewer opens and closes is remembered on their device.

app__menu_search.label: Search box
app__menu_search.description: A search box over the menu - by an entry's label, its full name, its description or its group. Automatic: once a viewer sees more than 15 entries.

backups__enabled.label: Backups
backups__enabled.description: Backs the instance up on the schedule below, and lets an administrator Back up now. Off: no new backup - those made stay listed, to download or delete.

backups__schedule.label: Schedule
backups__schedule.description: When, as a cron expression in the instance's timezone (Settings › General › General). 0 3 * * *: every day at 03:00.

backups__keep.label: Backups to keep
backups__keep.description: The most recent completed backups kept; an older one is deleted after each new one completes.

backups__destination.label: Destination
backups__destination.description: Where new backups are written. A backup already made stays where it was written.

backups__local_path.label: Local backups path
backups__local_path.description: The directory local backups are written to - mount a volume there, on another disk than the database's.

backups__include_files.label: Include stored files
backups__include_files.description: The files Files keeps on the local disk go into each backup. Files kept in S3 storage never do - back the bucket up with the service's own versioning or replication.

themes.hint: A theme to start from - it replaces the CSS below, which stays yours to edit.

mcp.addressHelp: Where an agent connects - this instance's public URL and /mcp, the same port as the API.
mcp.tokenHelp: An administrator's personal access token of the Admin plane - the agent can do exactly what that administrator can, audited under it.
mcp.claudeCodeHelp: Run in the project folder, with the token in TOTALBASE_TOKEN.
mcp.mcpJsonHelp: Or this file in the project folder - the token is read from TOTALBASE_TOKEN.

backups.deleteBody: {name} and its archive are deleted. This cannot be undone.
backups.scheduleOff: Backups are off - turn them on to back up on a schedule or now. Those made stay below.
backups.emptyDescription: Back up now, or turn on scheduled backups below.
backups.masterKeyApart: A backup never holds the master key: keep it apart - restoring needs it.

restore.title: Restore a backup
restore.description: The backup of {when} ({name}): the commands that restore it, to run where the instance runs.
restore.what: Nothing runs from here. The next steps give the commands that restore this backup into a new, empty database and switch the instance to it:
restore.whatDatabase: The current database, {database}, is left as it is - switching back undoes the restore.
restore.whatFiles: The stored files go back to the backup's; the current ones are moved aside, never deleted.
restore.whatStopped: TotalBase is stopped while it runs: plan a short pause.
restore.whatSince: Whatever changed after {when} is not in the backup.
restore.masterKeyHelp: The instance must start with the master key this backup was taken with - TOTALBASE_MASTER_KEY, or master.key in its data volume. The restore checks it before writing anything.
restore.databaseHelp: Created empty for the backup. Lowercase letters, digits and _.
restore.userHelp: The role TotalBase connects as (POSTGRES_USER) - the new database's owner.
restore.postgresInComposeHelp: As in the installation guide's first setup: the database is created through its service.
restore.postgresElsewhereHelp: A managed service or a server of your own: whoever administers it creates the database.
restore.identifierError: Lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _.
restore.serviceError: A Compose service name: letters, digits, ., _ and -.
restore.sameDatabase: Use a new database - never the one in use.

steps.create: Create the empty database, as PostgreSQL's superuser:
steps.createSql: Have the empty database created, by someone with the right to - TotalBase's user can't:
steps.download: Download {name} into the folder you run the next commands from:
steps.restore: Restore the backup into the new database - it checks the master key, the versions and that the database is empty first:
steps.switch: In docker-compose.yml, point TotalBase at the new database:
steps.start: Start TotalBase - it applies any newer migration:
steps.rollback: Point TotalBase back at the previous database and put its files back:
